logging._comment: OPTIONAL. Mirror the fetcher's stderr logs into Splunk via HEC so the Ingest Health dashboard can show real ingest success/failure/duration. stderr is ALWAYS on regardless of this block. With method=hec the logs go to EACH target's own HEC (reusing its hec_url + hec_token) into hec_logging_index - so every Splunk you feed sees its OWN ingest health. Override the endpoint with hec_logging_url / hec_logging_token if you must. NOTE: each target's HEC token must have write access to BOTH its data index AND hec_logging_index (one token, two indexes). Provision hec_logging_index (e.g. wearables_log) once per Splunk so logs can carry a shorter retention than health data. Remove this block to log to stderr only.

source._comment: UNLIKE the API-pull TAs, TA-apple WATCHES A FOLDER: Health Auto Export drops JSON there (usually synced down from Google Drive / iCloud by rclone - see INSTALL.md step 2). ONE shared source block feeds ALL targets below: each file is read once, fanned out to every target, and cleaned up ONCE (only after all targets succeed). min_file_age_seconds avoids reading a file still being written/synced. Set archive_dir to keep originals instead of deleting (delete_after_ingest then only removes the copy from watch_dir).

personal._comment: skip_sources drops data whose mapped vendor you ALSO pull via its own direct TA, to avoid double-representing the same measurement through two pipelines. START with [] (ingest EVERYTHING - 'Apple hub' mode) so your first run definitely produces data; once it is flowing, add the vendors you pull directly (e.g. ["oura","withings"]). hr_firehose (default false) admits Apple's per-sample heart_rate stream - high volume, only enable if you want intraday HR from Apple rather than a direct TA. person_id is REQUIRED for RBAC - register it in the wearables app first (Admin > People).
